## What I did

A preparatory, behavior-preserving refactor that carves out the seams the identity redesign will slot into. I did **not** implement the change.

**`Owner.java` — separated region derivation from its exposure**
- Split `getLocality()` into two: `getLocality()` is now the thin exposed accessor, delegating to a new `regionForOwner()` that holds the actual postcode-then-city derivation.
- This is the key seam: today both are the same region, but the change makes locality read the `REGION` out of the new `customerCode` while `regionForOwner()` remains the "compute region from the owner's fields" step used to *build* that code. Splitting them now means the change edits one focused method instead of overloading `getLocality`.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java` — focused the identity-building path**
- Renamed `nextCustomerCode(city, lastName)` → `customerCode(Owner owner)`, passing the whole owner so the builder can reach any (already-normalised) field the new `<REGION>-<HASH8>` scheme needs (telephone, last name, region) without disturbing the `addOwner` call site.
- Extracted the create-audit log statement into `auditOwnerCreated(owner)`, giving the audit format the single home the change will modify and trimming `addOwner`.
- Relocated an orphaned Javadoc block (it had drifted above `cityIsAtCapacity`) back onto the customer-code method and updated it.

The membership number, check digit, and audit already read `customerCode`, so they follow the new identity automatically — no structural prep was needed there.

## Test status — please note

The only test in the repo, `AcceptanceTest.coreCustomerCodeIsRegionHash`, is the **acceptance test for the upcoming change itself** — it asserts `customerCode` matches `<REGION>-<HASH8>`. It was already failing before I started (current code produces `TOW-SUR-0001`), and it still fails for the exact same reason, because I was instructed not to implement the change. There were no passing tests to keep green; my refactor introduced no new failures or compile errors, and every derived value is unchanged.
